chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Khalid al-Kufi, raising it to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: Worship has seventy parts, the most superior of which is seeking the lawful.

key_terms.الْعِبَادَةُ: Worship/devotion — encompasses all acts of obedience to God, not limited to ritual prayer
key_terms.سَبْعُونَ جُزْءًا: Seventy parts — Arabic rhetorical device indicating completeness or many divisions, not necessarily a literal count
key_terms.طَلَبُ الْحَلَالِ: Seeking the lawful — pursuing permissible earnings through honest work and trade

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about seeking halal livelihood as worship?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is reported by Imam al-Baqir (AS) to have stated that worship encompasses seventy divisions, and the highest of these is the pursuit of halal (lawful) livelihood. This hadith elevates the act of earning through lawful means to the apex of devotion, situating economic virtue at the heart of Islamic worship. In the early Islamic community, where livelihoods were often precarious and unlawful gains tempting, this teaching powerfully reframed honest work as the greatest form of piety.
